proof.text: Put $f=q|_K$ and $x=q(*)$, and let $\alpha:f\to\Delta_Kx$ be the specified coherent cocone. The functor $p:\mathcal C\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration: a lifting problem for an inner horn is just an inner horn in $\mathcal C$, which has a filler since $\mathcal C$ is a quasicategory; the filler lies over the given simplex because $\Delta^0$ has a unique simplex in every degree.

source.place: Inner horn and inner-fibration definitions; direct terminal-base argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] to $D=\mathcal C$, $B=\Delta^0$, this $p$, the given small $K$, and the given $q$. Its associated cocone is exactly $\alpha$: both are obtained using the same map $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$. It says that $q$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if, for every vertex $z$ of $\mathcal C$, the square with top row $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(f,\Delta_Kz)$, sending $u$ to $\Delta_K(u)\alpha$, and bottom row $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^0}(*,*)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\Delta^0)}(pf,\Delta_K*)$ is a homotopy pullback. That lemma applies to any functor and imposes no colimit-existence hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, equivalence of all-diagram and constant-target tests, in the apex form stated by lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test.

proof.text: For every simplicial set $L$, the definition $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\Delta^0)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(L\times\Delta^n,\Delta^0)$ gives one simplex in every degree. The same is true of the right-pinched mapping spaces in $\Delta^0$, so both spaces in the bottom row of step 2 are literally $\Delta^0$. Their path object also has one simplex in every degree. Consequently the path-pullback model for this square is $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(f,\Delta_Kz)\times_{\Delta^0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\Delta^0)\times_{\Delta^0}\Delta^0$, identified degreewise with its first factor. Under this identification the comparison is exactly $u\mapsto\Delta_K(u)\alpha$. Thus the square is a homotopy pullback precisely when this map is a weak homotopy equivalence. The unique coherence path in the bottom-right point contributes no additional data.

source.place: Terminal specialization of the explicit path-pullback definition; all identifications are degreewise.

proof.text: The cocone dual of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that $\alpha:f\to\Delta_Kx$ is colimiting precisely when $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(f,\Delta_Kz)$, $u\mapsto\Delta_K(u)\alpha$, is an equivalence for every $z$. This is the very condition obtained in steps 2 and 3, so it proves both implications. Its criterion uses arbitrary small shapes and specified cocones, without requiring other colimits. In particular, for $K=\varnothing$ the functor category on $K$ is a point, and the condition is that every $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,z)$ be contractible, exactly initiality of $x$. Thus no nonempty-shape assumption entered the proof.

title: Absolute colimits are colimits relative to the terminal quasicategory
statement: Use the coherent functor, mapping-space, cone and cocone conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the relative colimit notion of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory, let $K$ be a small simplicial set, and let $q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ be any diagram. Put $p:\mathcal C\to\Delta^0$ for the unique functor. Here, for a diagram $q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ with $f=q|_K$ and apex $x=q(*)$, its cocone is the coherent transformation $f\to\Delta_Kx$ obtained by precomposing $q$ with the map $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$ that keeps the vertices labelled $0$ in $K$ and sends the vertices labelled $1$ to the cone point; $q$ is called colimiting when this cocone is initial in the coherent cocone category. Then $p$ is an inner fibration, and $q$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if $q$ is colimiting in $\mathcal C$. No existence of other colimits in $\mathcal C$ is assumed; $K$ may be empty.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19 (02X1), constant-target test and colimit dual, specialized to the terminal base; cocone criterion in lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags. Read online, archival source WANTED.
